Now I understand the game! Clicking on the white palette block:
1. Changed the purple block in the gray frame to white (Node 12: color p->W)
2. Moved the white indicator strip from under the purple block to under the white block (Node 8 moved from cols 41-45 to cols 35-39)
So the top-right panel is a color selector. Clicking a color selects it and applies it to the framed block. The white strip indicates which color is selected.
Now the pattern is:
- Top-left reference: white on top, purple on bottom
- Main area: white in frame, purple strip, white strip
So I need to:
1. Select white (done) - the framed block is now white

3. Use SPACE to apply the color to the blocks below

<parameter=code>
# Clicking the white palette block changed the framed block to white!
# The white indicator strip moved under the white palette block.
# Now let me click the purple palette block to select purple

print("Probing: click on purple palette block (row 4, col 43)")
result = action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 4, 'col': 43}])
print("Result:", result)

# Check changes
before = last_transition.before_frame.segmentation
after = last_transition.after_frame.segmentation
before_nodes = {n['id']: n for n in before['nodes']}
after_nodes = {n['id']: n for n in after['nodes']}

print("\n=== CHANGES ===")
for nid in sorted(set(list(before_nodes.keys()) + list(after_nodes.keys()))):
    bn = before_nodes.get(nid)
    an = after_nodes.get(nid)
    if bn is None or an is None or bn['pixels'] != an['pixels'] or bn['boundary'] != an['boundary'] or bn['color'] != an['color']:
        if bn is None:
            print(f"  Node {nid} appeared: color={an['color']}, pixels={an['pixels']}")
        elif an is None:
            print(f"  Node {nid} disappeared: color={bn['color']}, pixels={bn['pixels']}")
        else:
            print(f"  Node {nid}: color {bn['color']}->{an['color']}, pixels {bn['pixels']}->{an['pixels']}")

# Check current state
ascii_lines = current_frame.ascii.split('\n')
print("\n=== Main area blocks ===")
for i in range(24, 44):
    line = ascii_lines[i][20:44]
    if any(c != 'B' for c in line):
        print(f"Row {i:2d}: {line}")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
